verses.sanskrit: नारद उवाच।  सुहोत्रं नाम राजानं मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम।  एकवीरमशक्यं तममरैरभिवीक्षितुम् ॥१॥
verses.english: Narada said O Srinjaya, we heard also of the death of king Suhotra, who was the foremost of all heroes, invincible and interviewed by the gods themselves.
verses.bhavadeepa: तुभ्यं तव । मरुत्तात्त्वं निर्गुणस्त्वत्तोऽपि निर्गुणस्त्वत्पुत्र इति न तदर्थं शोको युक्त इति भावः । अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यं पुत्रमभिलक्ष्य माऽनुतप्यथाः । हे श्वैत्य श्वित्यपुत्र इति 'व्याहरन्नारदः सृञ्जयं प्रतीति व्यासवाक्यम् ॥५०॥

verses.sanskrit: यः प्राप्य राज्यं धर्मेण ऋत्विग्ब्रह्मपुरोहितान्।  अपृच्छदात्मनः श्रेयः पृष्ट्वा तेषां मते स्थितः ॥२॥
verses.english: Having obtained his kingdom by virtue, he used to question his Ritvigas, family priests and Brahmanas about its welfare and then used to live up to their instructions.

verses.sanskrit: प्रजानां पालनं धर्मो दानमिज्या द्विषज्जयः।  एतत्सुहोत्रो विज्ञाय धर्मेणैच्छद्धनागमम् ॥३॥
verses.english: Knowing virtue to be identified with the protection of his subjects, acts of charity and performance of sacrifices and the subjugation of foes, Suhotra desired the increase of his wealth,

verses.sanskrit: धर्मेणाराधयन्देवान् बाणैः शत्रून् जयंस्तथा। सर्वाण्यपि च भूतानि स्वगुणैरप्यरञ्जयत् ॥४॥
verses.english: He worshipped the gods according to the ordinances of the holy texts and conquered his foes by means of his arrows. He pleased all creatures with his own excellent acquirements.

verses.sanskrit: यो भुक्त्वेमां वसुमतीं म्लेच्छाटविकवर्जिताम्। यस्मै ववर्ष पर्जन्यो हिरण्यं परिवत्सरान् ॥५॥
हैरण्यास्तत्र वाहिन्यः स्वैरिण्यो व्यवहन् पुरा। ग्राहान् कर्कटकांश्चैव मत्स्यांश्च विविधान् बहून् ॥६॥
verses.english: In those days of his the rivers ran liquid gold and were open to the use of everybody. Parjanya then poured on his kingdom large numbers of golden alligators, crabs and fishes of various classes and many other objects of desire; the artificial lakes of his dominions were full two miles long.

verses.sanskrit: कामान् वर्षति पर्जन्यो रूपाणि विविधानि च। सौवर्णान्यप्रमेयाणि वाप्यश्च क्रोशसंमिताः ॥७॥
verses.bhavadeepa: हैरण्या हिरण्मयाः ग्राहादयोऽपि वाहिन्यो नद्यः स्वैरिण्यः सर्वजनोपयोग्याः ॥६॥

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रं वामनान् कुब्जान्नक्रान् मकरकच्छपान्। सौवर्णान् विहितान् दृष्ट्वा ततोऽस्मयत वै तदा ॥८॥
verses.english: Then king Suhotra beholding thousands of dwarfs hunch-backs, alligators and sharks and tortoises, all made of gold, was greatly amazed.

verses.sanskrit: तत् सुवर्णमपर्यन्तं राजर्षिः कुरुजाङ्गलेः।  ईजानो वितते यज्ञे ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ह्यमन्यत ॥९॥
verses.english: That royal sage, having performed a sacrifice in Kurujangala, gave away that unlimited quantity of gold to the Brahmanas, even before the accomplishment of that sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit: सोऽश्वमेधसहस्रेण राजसूयशतेन च।  पुण्यैः क्षत्रिययज्ञैश्च प्रभूतवरदक्षिणैः ॥१०॥
काम्यनैमित्तिकाजस्रैरिष्टां गतिमवाप्तवान्। स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया ॥११॥
verses.english: And also having accomplished numerous daily rites from specific wishes, that king ultimately attained to a very desirable end. O Srinjaya, when even such a king suffered death, who was superior to you in all the four virtues.

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रान् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः।  अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभिश्वैत्येति व्याहरन् ॥१२॥
verses.english: And so was superior to your son, you should not lament for your son saying 'O Shvaitya' who performed no sacrifice and gave away no sacrificial presents.
